title: Horizon smoothing and critical-role rotations
creator: Talia Morgan
description: Create a playbook and lightweight tooling to smooth planning horizons across product cycles by introducing a rolling 'stability horizon' and an explicit critical-role rotation policy. The goal is to reduce mid-cycle disruption caused by ad hoc reallocations, make scope cuts predictable, and preserve delivery velocity for high-risk initiatives. Deliverables: 1) decision matrix for horizon cuts, 2) staffing rotation schedule and guardrails for critical roles, 3) a triage rubric for rapid scope reductions, and 4) an infra/PM checklist for handoffs when rotations occur.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc published in Confluence with versioned examples and 3 sample scenarios (hit, over-commit, emergent incident)
Rotation schedule prototype added to the staffing spreadsheet with automated conflict detection
Triage rubric accepted by Eng leads and Design; documented thresholds for automatic scope trims
Two dry-run simulations executed during the cycle and retrospective notes captured
Integration hooks defined for Console dashboards to surface 'stability horizon' signal (team-level capacity metric)
notes: Motivation: recurring mid-cycle reassignments to incident response and sales enablement have increased context switching and led to >15% slippage on committed deliverables over last 4 cycles.

Key trade-offs: longer stability horizons increase risk of missing emergent customer needs; shorter horizons reduce predictability. Playbook will recommend default 3-week horizon with adjustable knobs per initiative priority.
Design constraint: rotating people out of critical roles must maintain a blast radius <= 2x week-of-impact; handoffs must include documented runbooks and 1:1 overlap where feasible.
Operational tie-ins: integrate with on-call rota changes (ENG) and with staffing pool signals from People Ops for temporary backfills.
Draft metric: 'Horizon Volatility' = % of FTE reassignments impacting committed cycle scope; target < 8% by end of next two cycles.
